body: **Summary:** Indian pharma has four engines. US generics are a volume game with structural price erosion, where profit comes from limited-competition launches (first-to-file, complex injectables, inhalers, peptides). India branded formulations are a distribution and doctor-franchise business compounding at ~8–11%. APIs are cost and chemistry plays. CDMO/CRDMO runs multi-year molecule contracts with innovators. Key metrics: US sales ($) and price erosion, ANDA pipeline and approvals, USFDA inspection status (OAI, warning letters), India business growth against IPM (AIOCD/IQVIA), R&D % of sales, EBITDA margin, specialty share; for CDMO, order book, commercial molecules and capacity utilisation. Cycle drivers: US pricing cycles (consolidation of US buyers 2015–18 caused heavy erosion), FDA compliance waves (2014–19), one-off blockbuster generics (gRevlimid FY23–26), China API pricing, US policy (Section 232: 100% tariff on patented drugs from Apr 2026, generics exempt 'at this time') and the Biosecure Act shift away from Chinese CDMOs. Lead indicators: USFDA warning letters and 483s, the FDA Orange Book and drug-shortage list, AIOCD monthly IPM growth, IQVIA, China API prices. Winners (Sun after specialty, Torrent in India branded, Divi's in custom synthesis) built moats beyond plain generics and kept a clean compliance record. Losers were buried by FDA import alerts (Ranbaxy 2008–13, Wockhardt 2013) or debt-funded US acquisitions (Lupin's Gavis). Valuation: P/E ~20–35x, peaking in 2015 and Aug 2020 and troughing in 2018–19. Nov 2026: pharma is the only large-cap sector above its FY26 average valuation. Traps: one-product earnings and FDA risk. Sources: [1](https://upstox.com/news/market-news/stocks/dr-reddy-s-torrent-pharma-zydus-life-pharma-stocks-to-post-resilient-growth-in-q2-earnings-despite-pricing-headwinds/article-201775/) · [2](https://www.sahi.com/news/sun-pharma-anticipates-pricing-challenges-in-upcoming-quarters-1685-PE1_COR) · [3](https://www.india-briefing.com/news/us-patented-pharma-tariff-2026-india-generic-drug-exports-exempted-43899.html) · [4](https://www.crowell.com/en/insights/client-alerts/trump-administration-imposes-section-232-tariffs-on-patented-pharmaceutical-imports-tiered-rate-structure-takes-effect-beginning-july-31-2026) · [5](https://www.pharmexec.com/view/president-trump-phased-drug-tariff)

body:
Five Below sells "trend-right" goods to tweens, teens and "the kid in all of us", "most priced at $5 and below". The category worlds are Candy, Style, Party, Room, Create, Tech, Sports and New & Now. A typical store holds 4,000+ SKUs. Sales mix FY25: leisure 44.5%, fashion & home 30.9%, snack & seasonal 24.6% `[10K25 Item 1]`.
- **Stores:** 1,921 at FY25 end in 46 states, **all leased**, ~4% in malls; the rest are in power, community and lifestyle centres. There are 2,022 stores at Q2 FY26 `[PR-Q2 FY26]`.
- **Openings:** 228 gross in FY24 and 157 gross / 150 net in FY25. About 150 net are planned for FY26, and a first "handful" in Puerto Rico in H2 2027 `[CC-Q2FY26]`.
- **Long-run target:** "more than 3,500 locations over time" `[10K25]`.
- **Sourcing:** ~1,000 vendors; none >5% of purchases; **~60% of purchases from domestic vendors** (FY24 and FY25 alike). "China [is] the single largest source of merchandise we import **and source from domestic vendors**" `[10K25 Item 1A]`.
title: FIVE_practice › 1.1 The business in one paragraph

body:
**Why.** memdb `insight:lit-pead-post-earnings-drift`: Bernard–Thomas (1989) found ~4% top-minus-bottom
SUE-decile drift over 60 trading days in the US; Martineau (2022) shows it has vanished in US large/mid caps
and survives in microcaps. India has thin analyst coverage below the top ~300 names, results scattered over
~45 days and filed as PDFs — plausible conditions for underreaction. No academic Indian study was found in our
literature sweep. Bar for an "edge": `insight:lit-harvey-liu-zhu-multiple-testing` (t > 3, or out-of-sample).
Hygiene copied from `research_notes/Backtests/insider_clusters_us.md` (L14: matched controls, date at filing,
survivorship audit, pre-registered subgroups).

**Hypotheses.**
- **H1 (primary).** Stocks in the top SUE quintile out-perform stocks in the bottom SUE quintile over the
  63 trading days (≈3 months) after entry. H0: mean top-minus-bottom (T−B) = 0.
- **H2 (primary, long-only relevance).** Top-quintile stocks out-perform size-matched controls over 63 days.
- **H3 (pre-registered split).** The T−B spread is larger in the smallest mcap tertile (proxy for low analyst
  coverage) than in the largest tertile.

**Surprise measure (fixed).**
- Primary: **SUE (EPS)** from a seasonal random walk: `SUE_q = (EPS_q − EPS_{q−4}) / sd(ΔEPS over the
  previous 8 quarters)`, where ΔEPS_k = EPS_k − EPS_{k−4}, using only changes known before quarter q
  (k = q−1 … q−8). Require ≥ 4 prior changes (sd over what exists, up to 8); require sd > 0.
  EPS = basic EPS as reported for the quarter (consolidated if the company files consolidated results,
  else standalone; the same basis throughout for a company). Quarters with EPS restated later: use the
  figure in the filing for that quarter (first-reported where available).
- Secondary: **revenue SUE**, same formula on quarterly revenue from operations (per share not needed: the
  scale cancels in the ratio).
- Winsorise SUE at ±10 before ranking is not needed (ranks only); SUE is used only for ranking.

**Event date (fixed).** The NSE (or BSE if NSE missing) broadcast/filing timestamp of the quarterly result.
Entry = **adjusted close on the first NSE trading day strictly after the broadcast date** (so a result filed
during market hours or after the close is fully public before entry; this sacrifices the day-1 reaction,
on purpose — it is what we could actually trade). Secondary (context only): entry at the next-day open.

**Portfolios (fixed).** Cross-sections = fiscal quarter of the result (e.g., all Q3 FY24 results, quarter
ended 31-Dec-2023). Within each fiscal quarter, rank eligible events by SUE into **quintiles (primary)**
and deciles (secondary). Event-time returns: each stock enters on its own entry date. Portfolio return for a
quarter = equal-weighted mean of member returns. T−B per quarter = mean(top) − mean(bottom).
Horizons: **21, 63, 126 trading days** (≈1, 3, 6 months). Primary horizon = 63 days.

*Method calibration, not stock picking. Research, not SEBI-registered advice.*
Started 2026-11-23. Builds **stage 2 (hard filters) and stage 3 (signals) together**, feeding **stage 6** (the decision
card's avoid gate, `tools/decision/decision_card.py`). Lesson L31: after a bottom-two-quintile result, firms that later
landed on a distress list lagged controls by −16.6% in 13 weeks (71 events, descriptive, picked by later fate). This
test asks the forward-looking version with flags known *at the event*: promoter pledge (graded red, L28,
`hard_filters_india_v2.md`) and interest cover / S5-India (`solvency_flags_india.md`).
**Unlocks:** if the combination is much worse than either flag alone, the decision card gets a stronger
"miss + red flag = exit / no entry" gate (and the live PEAD tracker can tag events with flags); if not, the two gates
stay independent and simple.

3. **Layers:** L2 (group ROIC/ROIIC re-derived), L3 (plant utilisation and capex per piece), L5 (votes, subsidies). Honest limit: no

body:
- **σ = 0.35 is too narrow on every panel**: the card's own 50% interval caught 12–35% of outcomes and its 80% interval
  53–65%. σ_class brings coverage to ~nominal on India non-fin and US (47–50% / 76–80%) and lifts the whole-distribution
  log score a lot. It still **fails the pre-registered rule**: on lenders the wider σ raises the model P(≤0.5x), which the
  left anchoring then mixes in at 50%, so P(≤0.5x) over-shoots (28.9% vs 25.2%) and Σ Brier worsens by 0.012. The lender
  LOCO test is harsh (cohort medians 0.60x vs 1.73x), but the rule was fixed in advance: **fix (4) is not adopted**. A
  re-test (e.g. σ_class with the ≤0.5x tail not double-counted) would need its own new pre-registration.
- **Two-sided anchoring passes**: P(≥3x) moves from 0.12–0.45× the realised rate to 0.56–0.72×, log score up on all three,
  Brier guard held (lenders +0.0002). Per the amended parent prereg this is **necessary, not sufficient**: adoption still
  waits for the near-term live calls (to 30-Sep-2027) not to get worse.
- **Not fixed by either:** P(blow-up) is under-predicted in every variant (10.5% vs 15.5%; 16.3% vs 27.1%; 10.1% vs
  15.3%): a 5% model blow-up at w = 0.5 only gets two-thirds of the way to the base rate. The predicted mean is below the
  realised mean in all variants (India 1.67–2.04 vs 2.24): the bear>bull scenario shape (fix 5) is part of this.
- Caveats: two/three start dates in a strong small-cap window (2016–2023); India R is price-only; the forecast is the same
  for every firm in a cohort, so this tests the card's *shape and dispersion*, not stock picking.

title: README › Past-promise ledger (credibility input; strict y: delivered = 1, else 0)

body:
- M0: y = a + b·(1/PE)  — earnings-yield form of "P/E alone" (also report y on log(PE) as a robustness line).
- M1: y = a + b·(1/PE) + c·y10  (equivalent to adding the gap: EY and y10 enter separately; c < 0 expected).
- M2: y = a + d·G  (gap alone).
- Primary comparison for H2: M1 vs M0 (does the bond yield add information beyond P/E?). M2 vs M0 reported too.
